item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 26, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China News Service: We noticed that China organized a side event on Japan’s abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs) in China on the sidelines of the 31st Session of Conference of the State Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) in the Hague, the Netherlands. Can you brief us on the relevant information? Guo Jiakun: On November 25, China organized a side event on Japan’s ACWs in China on the sidelines of the 31st Session of Conference of the State Parties to the CWC and briefed the delegates attending the meeting on the fact that Japan’s ACWs in China are large in quantity, severe in harm and slow in disposal. China stressed that early and complete destruction of these weapons is Japan’s due obligation under international law in accordance with the CWC. The destruction process is now seriously lagging behind schedule. The root cause is that Japan insists on its distorted view of history, fails to genuinely reflect on its war crimes, stays indifferent with the harm of chemical weapons, flouts international obligations, and invests insufficiently in this matter. OPCW’s Director-General Sabrina Dallafior, chairperson of the Executive Council permanent representative of Morocco Ambassador Mohamed Basri, and delegates from many countries pointed out that Japan’s ACWs in China pose the greatest practical impediment to the goal of a world free of chemical weapons. China once again urges Japan to earnestly assume its historical, political and legal responsibilities, faithfully fulfill the obligations under the CWC and the MOU between the two countries’ governments, comprehensively scale up its human resources and financial inputs, actively provide information on burial sites, and speed up end-to-end disposal process, so that the day will come sooner when the hazardous Japanese ACWs are destroyed completely and thoroughly, when the Chinese people no longer have to live on soil tainted by ACWs, when justice prevails in the international community, and when humanity lives in a world free of chemical weapons. Bloomberg: The U.S. has announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China and other economies. The rate of imports from China would rise to 20 percent according to the USTR. That would be in line with the country’s prior agreement with the Trump administration. But the U.S. also said that that rate could double to 40 percent if talks between the two countries fall apart. We wonder if the foreign ministry has any comment. Guo Jiakun: We’ve made clear China’s position yesterday. Tariff wars and trade wars serve no one’s interests. Relevant issues should be resolved through consultation on the basis of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit. So-called “industrial overcapacity” does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation. China and the U.S. need to jointly deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. China will continue doing what is necessary to defend its legitimate rights and interests. Reuters: A Canadian NATO intern arrested in Belgium on suspicion of espionage will be placed under electronic monitoring while awaiting trial. This was a Canadian national of Chinese origin. What is China’s response to this? Guo Jiakun: We are not familiar with the specifics you mentioned. AFP: Japan’s coast guard said today that they had warned two Chinese ships to leave waters near the disputed Senkaku or Diaoyu Islands. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this apparent incident. Guo Jiakun: Diaoyu Dao and its affiliated islands have always been part of China’s territory. The Japanese vessels illegally intruded into the territorial waters of Diaoyu Dao in an act of provocation. The move seriously violates China’s sovereignty and undermines stability in the waters off Diaoyu Dao. China has lodged stern representations with the Japanese side. China Coast Guard vessels took necessary control measures against the relevant vessels in accordance with law. China firmly safeguards its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. We urge the Japanese side to abide by the four-point principled consensus between China and Japan, stop all infringement activities and provocations, and take effective measures to prevent the recurrence of similar incidents. Beijing Daily: Recently, the 10th China-Africa Youth Festival was held in Beijing and Shaanxi and received extensive coverage by African media. Can you share more information about the event? Guo Jiakun: The China-Africa Youth Festival is a regular event under the framework of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. Ten consecutive editions have been held so far and the event is widely popular among young people from both China and Africa. Recently, the 10th festival was successfully held in Beijing and Shaanxi. More than 60 African youths visited the Museum of the Communist Party of China and the Yan’an Revolutionary Memorial Hall to learn about the party’s great journey, and visited the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, where they learned about China’s socialist consultative democracy. They also explored the rich heritage of the Chinese civilization at the Palace Museum, and visited high-tech companies to gain firsthand insight into the dynamism of China’s economy. Through a wide range of engaging activities, young people from both sides had in-depth and heartfelt exchanges, further strengthening their bonds of friendship. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Africa diplomatic relations and the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges. China stands ready to continue working with the African side to promote mutual learning and exchanges, deepen mutual understanding and friendship, advance our respective modernization drives, and together build a community with a shared future for humanity.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 25, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Associated Press of Pakistan: Today, China has successfully launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft, with a Pakistani astronaut making history as the first foreign guest to participate in the mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. How does the Chinese foreign ministry view the significance of this milestone in China’s space program, and what opportunities does it present for further strengthening space cooperation between Pakistan and China, particularly in areas such as astronaut training and joint space exploration? Guo Jiakun: Today, amid high expectation of our two peoples, the Chinese and Pakistani astronauts embarked on the journey to China’s Tiangong space station for historic space technology cooperation. It is the first time for China’s space station to welcome a foreign astronaut, marking a new milestone in international cooperation on China’s manned space program. As President Xi Jinping noted in his congratulatory message to Pakistani President Zardari, the joint spaceflight mission of Chinese and Pakistani astronauts epitomizes the profound friendship between our two countries and marks another important outcome of the bilateral cooperation. China’s space station is a space station of peace, friendship and cooperation. China will work with Pakistan and other countries to hold high the banner of peaceful use of outer space, deepen international cooperation on space programs, improve global space governance, and ensure that the outcomes of outer space exploration benefit all humanity. Exploring the space is our shared aspiration. China’s space station is not only a home in space for Chinese astronauts, but also a pilot platform for global scientific research. The joint spaceflight has expanded and injected fresh impetus into China-Pakistan all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. We stand ready to work with more countries willing to embrace cooperation to explore the vast space together. Global Times: The U.S. State Department issued a statement welcoming the joint bid by Chile and Belgium to host the Secretariat of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. Does China have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: The United States, neither a state party to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea nor to the BBNJ Agreement, has no say on the selection of the BBNJ Secretariat seat. We call on all parties to stay vigilant against attempts to politicize the bidding and create confrontation in the process. China has made clear its position on the Belgium-Chile proposal. This joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects, namely, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement, procedural justice, established international practice, equitable geographical distribution, fair competition and the original commitment. Let me stress once again that according to the BBNJ Agreement, the seat of the Secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM), including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by the Conference of the Parties, and the CHM shall be managed by the Secretariat. These are the consensus as well as rights and responsibilities of all Parties to the Agreement, which no country has the right or is in any position to violate. No one shall trade under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties, let alone coerce or hijack other Parties into accepting their proposal. As one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China stands ready to work with the international community to uphold the original purpose of the Agreement and keep the selection of the Secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, so that the BBNJ Agreement can truly serve the shared interests of humanity. Bloomberg: The U.S. is set to announce tariffs on goods from China and some other countries. The additional tariffs won’t lead to an overall rate that exceeds the agreed-upon levels, which were reached in individual trade talks earlier. Would China like to comment on these possible levies coming? Guo Jiakun: Our position on handling China-U.S. economic and trade issues is consistent and clear. Tariff wars and trade wars serve no one’s interests. Relevant issues should be resolved through consultation on the basis of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit. The so-called issue of “industrial overcapacity” does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation. China and the U.S. need to jointly deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. Reuters: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said today that a new treaty will strengthen Australia’s security partnership with the Solomon Islands. Has the Solomon Islands terminated its security pact with China? How will the new treaty affect China’s relations with the Solomon Islands? Guo Jiakun: We have made clear our position yesterday. The international community should help Pacific island countries realize sustainable development. At the same time, in developing relations with Pacific island countries, all countries need to respect their independence, put development first, and uphold openness and inclusiveness. Relevant cooperation should not target any third party. AFP: Thailand is holding talks on pollution from mines in Myanmar at the moment. Some of these mines are run by Chinese companies. Thailand has apparently asked for mining sites to close for six months. Does China support this request from Thailand and has China asked any Chinese companies to stop mine production in Myanmar? Guo Jiakun: As a friendly neighbor of Thailand and Myanmar, China follows closely the issue of water pollution in the Mekong tributary along the Thailand-Myanmar border. We stand ready to work with Thailand and Myanmar to enhance cooperation on water resources governance, share experience, strengthen capacity, and jointly protect the ecological environment of the Mekong River basin. We hope Thailand and Myanmar will make good use of the joint working group mechanism to conduct field investigations, to which China will send experts and provide technical support. I would also like to stress that the Chinese government always asks Chinese enterprises overseas to abide by local laws and regulations and opposes any act that harms the ecological environment. The issue of water pollution may involve multiple factors, including geological conditions, climate change and human activities. We should identify the root causes and take targeted measures in a science-based, professional and objective spirit, and refrain from jumping to conclusions or making hasty judgments.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 24, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Shenzhen TV: Recently, Vice President of the Swiss Federal Council and Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis paid a visit to China and had the fifth round of China-Switzerland Foreign Ministers’ Strategic Dialogue with Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi. Could you please share more information about this visit? Guo Jiakun: Switzerland is China’s important innovative strategic partner in Europe. The China-Switzerland relationship has always been at the forefront of China’s relationships with Western countries, and has become a good example for cooperation between countries with different social systems and at different development stages. On the occasion of the 10th anniversary of the China-Switzerland innovative strategic partnership, the President and the Vice President of the Swiss Federal Council paid visits to China within a month. These visits have shown high political trust of the two countries and forged broad consensus for cooperation. The Foreign Ministers’ Strategic Dialogue is an effective mechanism where Chinese and Swiss diplomatic authorities strengthen policy synergy and coordination on bilateral and multilateral affairs. Regarding the fifth round of this dialogue, China has released information. The two sides agreed to follow the important common understandings reached by the leaders, step up high-level engagements, uphold mutual respect, mutual trust, openness and cooperation, improve and upgrade cooperation in free trade, finance, innovation, education, people-to-people exchanges and other areas, strengthen communication on global AI governance and other issues, deepen multilateral coordination, safeguard international fairness and justice, and contribute to peace, stability, prosperity and progress of the world. Bloomberg: NVIDIA Corp.’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang less than two weeks after he left under a cloud of scandal. President Trump had pressed for the move and the board cited the U.S government’s input when making the announcement. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on Huang’s return? Guo Jiakun: We have no comment on this. AFP: On Monday, the United States added Singapore-based Megaspeed International to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips. This is related to the NVIDIA news because the alleged spy Jensen Huang had an affair with was an executive at Megaspeed. Regarding this trade blacklist, does the Chinese foreign ministry have a comment or response? Guo Jiakun: We have made clear China’s position on the relevant issue more than once. I have nothing further to add. Bloomberg: It’s reported that the Solomon Islands has informed China it is terminating the landmark security agreement when it expires. Can the foreign ministry confirm this and does the ministry have any comment about the report that the Solomon Islands will sign a new deal with Australia? Guo Jiakun: China always follows the principle of mutual respect and equality in developing relations with the Solomon Islands. There is no element of geopolitical rivalry or bloc confrontation in cooperation between China and Pacific island countries, including the Solomon Islands. Our cooperation does not target any third party and is not subject to third-party influence. The international community should pool efforts to help Pacific island countries realize sustainable development on the basis of respecting their independence, putting development first, and upholding openness and inclusiveness. Relevant cooperation should not target any third party. AFP: Yesterday, Ukraine claimed that it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off the coast of Libya. Does China have a comment on this latest development of war between Russia and Ukraine? Guo Jiakun: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China’s position on the Ukraine crisis has been consistent and clear. Bloomberg: We saw that a Pakistani Air Force pilot will blast off on China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft on Wednesday, becoming the first foreign astronaut in the history of China’s manned space program. We are wondering if the foreign ministry has any comment. Guo Jiakun: The joint mission of the Pakistani astronaut and the Chinese crew to Tiangong space station will mark the first of its kind in the history of China’s manned space program. The Pakistani astronaut will be the first visiting foreign astronaut to China’s space station. This year marks the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic ties. The joint mission will be yet another important milestone in the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. We look forward to their exciting journey into space. We wish the mission a full success.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 23, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands Tom Berendsen will visit China from November 23 to 25. CCTV: To follow up on your announcement that Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands Tom Berendsen will visit China, how does China assess its relations with the Netherlands? What is China’s expectation of the visit? Guo Jiakun: China and the Netherlands, both major economies in the world, are important cooperation partners. Over recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, the two countries have engaged in close high-level exchanges, made steady progress in practical cooperation in areas of agriculture, water conservation, environmental protection, and science and technology, and consistently deepened cultural and people-to-people exchanges. This will be Foreign Minister Berendsen’s first visit to China after taking office. China hopes to have in-depth exchanges of views with the Netherlands during the visit on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest, to enhance understanding and mutual trust, deepen cooperation in various areas, and promote the sustained, sound and steady development of the open and pragmatic partnership for comprehensive cooperation for greater benefit to both peoples. Anadolu Agency: About the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen last week, the leaders’ declaration was comprehensive in terms of scope affecting a wide range of issues about global governance. Do you think this Group 3 (G3) type of dialogue, if established as a regular mechanism, might weaken existing multilateral settings, considering that international organizations and other countries are left out of the table? Guo Jiakun: We have released information on the China-Russia-U.S. summit. China always maintains that all countries, big or small, are equal, and stays committed to fostering greater democracy in international relations and building an equal and orderly multipolar world. China does not engage in geopolitical rivalry and seeks no sphere of influence. What it pursues are friendly exchanges with all countries on the basis of mutual respect and equality. We will continue to practice true multilateralism and contribute to joint efforts towards building a community with a shared future for humanity. Polish Press Agency: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said last week that he will visit China in early December. Could the Chinese side confirm this and provide details? Against the backdrop of China-EU trade frictions and the Ukraine crisis, what concrete outcomes does China hope to achieve through this visit? Guo Jiakun: High-level exchanges are vital to the development of China-Poland relations. On the visit you mentioned, I have no information to share at the moment. China Daily: On November 22, 2021, President Xi Jinping and leaders of ASEAN countries held a special summit to commemorate the 30th anniversary of China-ASEAN dialogue relations and announced the elevation of the China-ASEAN relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. A few days ago, Premier Li Qiang attended the 29th China-ASEAN Summit, where both sides issued a joint statement on commemorating the 5th anniversary of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. How does China assess the cooperation over the past five years, and what are its expectations for the future development of China-ASEAN relations? Guo Jiakun: The establishment of the China-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership is a milestone in our bilateral relations. Over the past five years, under the strategic guidance of leaders on both sides, China and ASEAN have promoted the tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, upheld the fundamental principles of openness and mutual benefit, and embraced the trend of innovation-driven development. As a result, our pragmatic cooperation has reached a new height. Trade between the two sides last year exceeded US$1 trillion. The China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will soon enter into force. Major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung high-speed railway and the China-Laos railway have been implemented. And the Pinglu Canal has officially opened to navigation. Our two sides have successfully held the China-ASEAN Year of People-to-People Exchanges and implemented the “ASEAN Visa” program, further facilitating exchanges between the peoples. Solid progress has been made in building a community with a shared future between China and ASEAN countries both in bilateral and plurilateral formats, laying a solid foundation for building a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. This year marks the beginning of China’s 15th Five-Year Plan and the ASEAN Community Vision 2045. Next year will mark the 60th anniversary of the establishment of ASEAN. All these present important opportunities for the development of China-ASEAN relations. China will work with ASEAN countries to enhance solidarity and mutual trust, expand consensus on cooperation, build a robust China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0, and effectively implement the plan of action for the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. We stand ready to deepen cooperation in key fields such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, connectivity and energy security, jointly build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, and bring greater stability and certainty to regional peace and development. Reuters: The UN climate conference COP31 ended on Sunday without any deal, which many countries are saying is a disappointing outcome. What is China’s reaction to COP failing to arrive at a deal this year? Guo Jiakun: On November 22, the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change was concluded in Antalya, Türkiye. At the meeting, decisions were adopted on issues such as just transition, mitigation, adaptation and finance. The meeting, however, ended without an overarching political deal. Despite being somewhat disappointed, China believes there is no reason to lose faith in the multilateral process. Let me stress that tackling climate change requires global effort. Green and low-carbon transition is an irreversible trend. All parties need to commit to multilateralism, uphold the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, and find more political will and common ground to tackle climate change in solidarity and deliver the Paris Agreement on the basis of respecting multilateral rules, science and national realities. China made enormous effort to facilitate a successful COP31. President Xi’s Special Representative and Vice President Han Zheng attended the Antalya Leaders’ Summit, who reaffirmed China’s commitment to carbon peak and carbon neutrality and put forward China’s proposal on global climate governance in the national statement. The Chinese delegation played a constructive role as well by engaging fully and substantively in the negotiations, reaching out to relevant parties, and moving the course of the meeting in a positive direction. China is committed to multilateralism, international cooperation and green transition, and will continue to act responsibly, work with all parties to tackle challenges and difficulties and promote the green and low-carbon transition and sustainable development worldwide. Anadolu Agency: In the trilateral summit, leaders of China, the U.S. and Russia declared that they recognize the principle of state consent and respecting immunities of state officials and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. The ICC led investigations of war crimes and crimes against humanity and issued arrest warrants for Israel’s prime minister and former defense minister. Does China see these court orders as abuse of judicial power? What should the limits of immunity for state officials be regarding these cases? Guo Jiakun: On the Palestinian question, China supports all efforts that are conducive to realizing fairness and justice and upholding the authority of international law. China always maintains that the International Criminal Court should adhere to an objective and impartial stance, exercise its mandate in accordance with law, and interpret and apply the Rome Statute and general international law in their entirety, in good faith and in line with consistent standards. Anadolu Agency: Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that it was a mistake to talk about the Ukraine issue in a meeting where his country was not on the table. So my question is, in the trilateral summit, did the leaders talk about the situation in Ukraine? China’s position on the Ukraine crisis has been consistent and clear. We always believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the crisis, and support all efforts for peace. Reuters: The Chinese delegation at COP31 was mostly absent from public events during the two weeks of conference. Why has China chosen to have such a low-key presence? And why has China decided against hosting COP in 2028? Guo Jiakun: On your first question, as I just said, China has made enormous effort to facilitate a successful COP31. President Xi’s Special Representative and Vice President Han Zheng attended the Antalya Leaders’ Summit, who reaffirmed China’s commitment to carbon peak and carbon neutrality and put forward China’s proposal on global climate governance in the national statement. The Chinese delegation played a constructive role as well by engaging fully and substantively in the negotiations, reaching out to relevant parties, and moving the course of the meeting in a positive direction. As for your second question, I have no further information beyond our earlier response. Reuters: U.S. President Trump has said the U.S. wants to sell only older chips to China, and that his administration was in discussion with China about this. What is China’s reaction to that comment, and is China indeed engaging in such talks for older chips? Guo Jiakun: The Chinese side has made clear its position on U.S. export control measures. ***************************************** The following question was raised by Reuters after the press conference: It’s reported that Nepal plans to convene an international summit to raise money for reconstruction after the recent floods. Nepal said China has indicated its willingness to support the effort but hasn’t quantified that yet. Nepal also said China had agreed to share more early warning and climate data. Does the ministry have any comment? Guo Jiakun: China and Nepal are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers. In the wake of the large-scale mudslide disaster in northern Nepal, China immediately announced emergency assistance for the affected areas in Nepal and conducted international rescue cooperation. The Chinese government provided Nepal with cash assistance and five batches of emergency relief supplies, sent over 20 experts specializing in tunnel rescue and forensic identification, and continuously shared data on meteorological, hydrological and geological conditions. Meanwhile, people from various sectors in China also extended a helping hand, conveying their care and support to the people in Nepal. The disaster has caused severe damage, and reconstruction faces enormous challenges. China is closely following the developments and feels for Nepal over the disaster. On top of the emergency assistance already provided, China will actively support Nepal’s reconstruction effort to help people in the disaster-hit areas rebuild their homes and return work and life to normal as early as possible. China will also help Nepal improve capability in disaster prevention and mitigation to better address the risks and challenges brought by natural disasters.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 20, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
At the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore Gan Kim Yong, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore from November 22 to 23, and co-chair with Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong the 22nd meeting of the China-Singapore Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, the 27th meeting of the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park Joint Steering Council, the 18th meeting of the China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Joint Steering Council, and the 10th meeting of the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity Joint Steering Council. Xinhua News Agency: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. We notice that the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community put forward at the meeting has sparked heated discussion worldwide. Could you share more details on that? Guo Jiakun: On November 19, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. President Xi Jinping chaired the meeting and delivered important remarks, in which he elaborated on China’s proposals on building an Asia-Pacific community and announced China’s voluntary measures to support Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders’ Shenzhen Outlook—an ambitious, pragmatic and comprehensive document. This is the most important outcome of APEC “China Year,” and marks a new milestone in APEC cooperation. The Shenzhen Outlook focuses on four major areas “trade and economy, connectivity, innovation, and development,” and eight key aspects “Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, physical connectivity, institutional connectivity, people-to-people connectivity, digital economy, emerging technologies, capacity building, and sustainable growth,” setting up the pillars for building an Asia-Pacific community. The APEC members reaffirmed their commitment to APEC as the premier forum for regional economic cooperation, and to making continuous efforts to move toward the goal of building an Asia-Pacific community. They also extended their sincere appreciation to China, the host country, and the people and city of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province for their warm hospitality and thorough arrangements. China will work with Asia-Pacific partners to implement the common understandings reached at the meeting, work steadily toward the goal of Asia-Pacific community, strive for the wellbeing of the people in China and the Asia-Pacific, and make greater contributions to world peace and development. Asahi Shimbun: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said at a press conference in Shenzhen yesterday that the Japanese government’s position on the Taiwan question remains consistent with the 1972 Japan-China Joint Statement. She also indicated that there has been no change in the status of the four political documents between Japan and China, which serve as the foundational documents for bilateral relations. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: Abiding by the four political documents between China and Japan is the political responsibility and legal obligation that Japan must fulfill. This should be not just reflected in remarks, but more importantly, implemented with concrete actions. For Japan, the pressing priority is to correct the erroneous words and moves on the Taiwan question immediately, adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China. JoongAng Ilbo: Yesterday the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia held a successful summit in Shenzhen. It’s reported that China said the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges. How would China respond if the U.S. were to host a second trilateral summit during the G20 Miami Summit next month? Guo Jiakun: The China-Russia-U.S. Summit was successfully held yesterday. China has released a readout, which you may refer to. AFP: The United Nations International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar is guilty of genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. What is China’s comment on the ruling? Guo Jiakun: China has noted the judgment of the International Court of Justice. Given its complex historical, ethnic and religious dimensions, the Rakhine state issue needs to be resolved prudently through a holistic approach. The international community should make joint efforts to this end and avoid complicating the issue. China stands ready to continue supporting relevant parties in stepping up dialogue and consultation, and to play a constructive role in resolving the issue regarding the repatriation of the displaced people from Rakhine state. China believes international judicial institutions, as important instruments for upholding international fairness and justice, should exercise their powers with full prudence in accordance with law. China has concerns regarding such issues as ultra vires jurisdiction and overreach in interpretation, which are not conducive to the settlement of disputes. Global Times: The Chinese side just announced that Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore and co-chair the mechanism meetings on bilateral cooperation. Could you share more information on this? Guo Jiakun: China and Singapore are friendly neighbors and important cooperation partners. Under the strategic guidance of the leaders of both sides, China-Singapore relations have maintained a sound momentum of growth, yielding fruitful outcomes in cooperation across various fields. President Xi Jinping just had an important meeting with Prime Minister Lawrence Wong this morning, charting the course for a new stage of development for bilateral ties. The mechanism meetings on bilateral cooperation are the apex platform coordinating collaboration between our two countries. China stands ready to work with Singapore to make good use of the meetings to deliver on our leaders’ strategic common understandings, formulate coordinated plans for cooperation in the next phase, unlock fresh impetus for the modernization drive in both countries, seek greater progress in our all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, and contribute to development and prosperity in the region. AFP: This is a follow-up on the question about the International Court of Justice’s ruling on Myanmar. The Chinese ICJ jurist Xue Hanqin voted in Myanmar’s favor on all but one count. So my question is, was Ms. Xue acting on the instructions from the Chinese government? Guo Jiakun: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. Its judges serve in their individual capacity and perform their duties independently. Judge Xue Hanqin’s expression of her views is grounded in international law and the facts of the case, and informed by her expertise. This is consistent with the court’s established procedures and practices, and reflects the proper fulfillment of her responsibilities. Beijing Youth Daily: A total of ten foreign nationals received the Third Orchid Awards, according to selection results released by the Chinese side today. Would you like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We congratulate the laureates of the 2026 Orchid Awards. Hailing from all over the world, they share the same commitment to dispelling prejudice and nurturing understanding through cultural exchanges. Through decades of dedicated efforts, they have built bridges of friendship connecting the people of China and other countries. Established in 2022, the Orchid Awards have become an international cultural platform that delivers on the Global Civilization Initiative. China is ready to work with all parties to foster solidarity and enhance cooperation among different civilizations, cultures and peoples to seek common progress and build a community with a shared future for humanity. Asahi Shimbun: The China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace said that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. I have two questions. First, how would China define the “abuse” of jurisdiction? Second, what exactly do “other similar bodies” refer to? Guo Jiakun: On the International Criminal Court, China’s position is consistent, clear and above-board. China supports international judicial bodies in playing a constructive role for upholding international rule of law. That said, China stands that no international judicial body should violate the principle of state consent, abuse their jurisdiction, engage in politicization, or apply double standards.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 19, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Shenzhen TV: This morning, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was successfully held in Shenzhen. Could you share more details? Guo Jiakun: This morning, President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and delivered important remarks in Shenzhen. President Xi Jinping noted that the launch of APEC more than 30 years ago started a remarkable journey toward building an Asia-Pacific community. over three decades and more, the Asia-Pacific region has witnessed progress with each passing day, and created the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, we must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. President Xi Jinping stressed that China stands ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community: strengthen the pillar of economy and trade by aligning various regional economic and trade agreements and enhancing policy dialogue on the FTAAP; upgrade the pillar of connectivity by improving the infrastructure network, harmonizing policies and regulations, and facilitating travel for business, tourism and other purposes; foster the pillar of innovation by strengthening digital infrastructure development and encouraging the broad application of AI; enhance the pillar of development by promoting regional cooperation on energy and food security, achieving sustainable economic growth, supporting livelihood improvements, and investing in the people. President Xi announced new measures China would take to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, including providing financial support for APEC’s practical cooperation, establishing a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen, and setting up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of SMEs. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC leaders’ declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. AFP: Some South Korean media outlets have reported today that there are no signs of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visiting China. Can the foreign ministry give us an indication of whether a meeting between Kim and U.S. President Donald Trump in China is being arranged? Guo Jiakun: I do not have information on that. Asahi Shimbun: Regarding the arrangements for the APEC events, the pared-down welcome accorded to the Japanese Prime Minister has been interpreted by some as a snub and drawn quite some attention. What’s China’s consideration behind such arrangements? Guo Jiakun: As the host, China makes appropriate protocol arrangements for all participants in accordance with international practice. AFP: Will the Chinese leader hold a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi on the sidelines of the APEC summit? Guo Jiakun: Our position on China-Japan relations is clear.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on November 18, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
CCTV: The 2026 APEC CEO Summit is held in Shenzhen today, which is attended by many state leaders and people from the business communities. Can you share more details about this event? Guo Jiakun: This morning, President Xi Jinping attended the opening ceremony of the 2026 APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen and delivered a keynote speech, in which he made four propositions for jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and bringing prosperity for all in the region. First, upholding peace and stability. We should uphold the postwar international order and promote an equality-based and orderly multipolar world and economic globalization that is inclusive and brings benefit to all. We should resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. This is the way to cement the foundation for sustaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. Second, building bridges of opening up and cooperation. We should firmly safeguard the WTO-centered, rules-based multilateral trading system, support free and open trade and investment, and keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. We should work steadily toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific to pave the way for greater economic integration in the region. Third, boosting innovation to drive growth. We should forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. Fourth, expanding our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. We should remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy. At the same time, we should promote development that is balanced and delivers benefit to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness. We should follow a people-centered development philosophy, and ensure that development fruits are shared by all economies and all groups and communities. China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to help explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. President Xi pointed out that China’s economy maintains a strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, demonstrating great resilience and vitality. A blueprint for China’s development, the 15th Five-Year Plan also provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. China will provide global business communities with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, and an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. Asia-Pacific business communities are more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China’s reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization. AFP: Regarding tomorrow’s trilateral meeting between the three presidents of China, Russia and the U.S., will it cover Ukraine? Trump said before leaving for Asia that the leaders would talk about Ukraine. So would China shut down any discussion of Ukraine if it comes up? Guo Jiakun: The three heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace. We will release information about the summit in a timely manner. Please check back for updates. The Hindu: I know you said previously that China hopes the meeting will focus on promoting strategic stability among the major powers. I was just wondering could you elaborate if are there any expectations of concrete outcomes that China hopes to see? Guo Jiakun: China has shared information on the China-Russia-U.S. Shenzhen Summit. The three heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace. We will release information about the summit in a timely manner. Please check back for updates. AFP: The interim CEO of NVIDIA told shareholders yesterday that it was no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China, which means that the H200 chips that were previously allowed into China under a deal by Washington are no longer being sent over. Does China have a comment on this? Guo Jiakun: We have made clear more than once our principled position on U.S. chip exports to China.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on the 7.6 Magnitude Earthquake in Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Q: It’s reported that a 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama on October 10, followed by over 100 aftershocks. What is China’s comment? A: China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there is no report of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and promptly provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need. We remind Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.
